caveats: ⚑ TRIGGER IDENTIFIER UNVERIFIED: the full-charge phase-counter trigger's union member was REDACTED from the packet's types.ts copy (only its comment survived). Authored as {kind:'fullChargeCount', count:[3,6,9]}; the real identifier and field name/arity MUST be read from src/skills/types.ts before this file will pass validate-overrides.

⚑ COUNT SEMANTICS: counts written as the kit PRINTS them (cumulative full-charge count per phase: 3/6/9 base, 1/2/3 under burst). If the engine's array is per-phase INCREMENTS instead, base becomes [3,3,3] and the burst variant [1,1,1].

⚑ BURST COUNT-CHANGE ENCODING: no EffectDef can mutate the required charge count, so the burst line is modeled STRUCTURALLY as a third skill1 block (fbGate inFb + ownBurstGate cast) carrying the reduced counts, with the base counts split across outFb and inFb+notCast blocks. Consequence: the ONE real phase counter is fragmented into THREE independent counters, and the 10 s buff window is approximated by the Full Burst window.

⚑ PHASE CYCLE: kit is silent on what happens after the 9-charge phase. Assumed the phase counter WRAPS (next 3 charges re-fire phase 1). If it instead latches at phase 3, every post-wrap 283.03%/565% hit here is an over-credit.

⚑ DISTRIBUTED DAMAGE: 565% / 848.03% are 'Distributed Damage' lines; against the single partless scope-lock boss they are modeled at FULL magnitude with no split. Correct if distribution divides among enemies hit; an over-credit if the game applies a per-target fraction even at n=1.

⚑ CRIT ELIGIBILITY: all three riders set crit:true per the rider prior (riders crit at the caster's sheet rate). Distributed-damage crit behaviour is UNMEASURED — read popup colours before trusting it.
core:false on the 283.03% hit — the text says 'as damage', not 'core strike damage' (no core bucket for riders absent that wording).

override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Blind second read of the kit prose only (no board access, no driver artifacts). RL/Wind/Attacker/B3, ammo 9, chargeFrames 18, reloadFrames 152. Damage lives entirely in skill1's full-charge phase cycle (283.03% single-target → 565% distributed → 848.03% distributed); the burst contributes no damage of its own but triples phase throughput (charge count 3/6/9 → 1/2/3) on top of ATK ▲115.12% and Charge Damage ▲169.63% for 10 s, and skill2's Max Ammo ▲60% + full reload at Full Burst entry is a DAMAGE line (it buys extra full charges, i.e. extra phases). The burst's count-change is encoded structurally as an fbGate/ownBurstGate block split because no EffectDef can mutate a trigger threshold — see caveats for the counter-fragmentation cost. Full-charge cadence (chargeFrames/reloadFrames/ammo) is the single most load-bearing unmeasured input: it sets how many phases fire per fight, so a cadence error scales total damage almost linearly.

flags.reasoning: The packet's types.ts copy has the full-charge phase-counter trigger's union member REDACTED — only its comment survived ('each full charge advances a phase counter; phase P fires block.effects[P]... OR a per-phase array (PREFERRED — the datamined "attack count required"...)'). So the mechanic is certain but the identifier, field name and cumulative-vs-increment convention are guesses. Counts are written as the kit prints them (3/6/9 and 1/2/3), matching the 'attack count required' datamine phrasing.
flags.recipe: Read the redacted union member in src/skills/types.ts, rename the kind and field to match, then run validate-overrides. To pin the convention, log damage events and count full charges to the first 283.03% hit: 3 charges ⇒ cumulative array; 3 charges to phase 1 then 3 more to phase 2 is consistent with both, so use phase 3 as the discriminator (9 total charges ⇒ cumulative; 6 total ⇒ increments).

flags.estimate: 3-block split: outFb base / inFb+notCast base / inFb+cast reduced; 10 s buff window ≈ the FB window
flags.reasoning: The burst line changes a TRIGGER THRESHOLD, which no EffectDef can express. The split keeps the reduced counts scoped to rotations this unit actually bursts (ownBurstGate 'cast' — a bare inFb gate would over-credit in multi-B3 comps) and keeps base counts alive during teammate-driven FBs (a bare outFb gate would silently drop all skill1 phases there). Cost: the one real phase counter becomes three independent counters, so phases banked in one gate state do not carry into another.
flags.recipe: Confirm the engine truly has no threshold-mutating primitive (grep types.ts/sim.ts for the phase-counter field). If a first-class 'count override while buffed' path exists, collapse to a single block. Then measure: log full charges + skill1 damage events across one burst window on a comp where she is the sole B3, and check the phase sequence resumes rather than restarts at FB exit.

flags.estimate: counter wraps after phase 3 (charges 10-12 re-fire phase 1, etc.)
flags.reasoning: The kit states only three tiers and 'only one effect is triggered at a time'; it never says what happens past nine charges. A wrapping cycle is the standard reading of this kit shape, but a latch-at-max reading is possible and would REMOVE most 283.03%/565% procs in a long fight.
flags.recipe: Count skill1 popups over a full 3-minute fight and bucket them by magnitude. Wrap predicts roughly equal counts of the three tiers; latch predicts one 283.03%, one 565%, then 848.03% repeating.

flags.estimate: as datamined: 18-frame full charge (0.30 s), 152-frame reload (2.53 s), 9-round magazine
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑: datamined cadence fields are known-unreliable, and here the cadence IS the damage curve — every phase proc is bought with full charges, so a 10% cadence error moves total damage ~10%. RL charge-shot cadence also has to respect 60 fps frame boundaries (effective = 60/ceil(60/nominal)), which the raw field does not.
flags.recipe: Read the ammo counter on a recorded fight to get shots/sec directly (the instrument that measures the disputed quantity), and time reload-start → first-shot for the reload frames; compare against the datamined tuple before tuning any magnitude.

flags.estimate: full stated magnitude (565% / 848.03%) against the single boss, no split factor
flags.reasoning: 'Distributed Damage' divides a total among the enemies hit; with exactly one enemy the whole amount should land, but the engine has no distributed-damage channel and the game may still apply a per-target fraction. This is the largest single magnitude risk in the file (848.03% is the biggest number in the kit).
flags.recipe: Read the popup value for a 565% proc off a recorded fight, divide by the sheet-computed 565%-of-final-ATK expectation with buffs snapshotted at that frame, and check whether the ratio is ~1.0 or a clean fraction.
